title: Savile Row — the whole subject is 280 metres
subtopic: S1 — Savile Row: 280 metres, and where the trade came from
learning_goal: Know how short the street is, that the trade clustered here by accident of customers, that its root is uniform, and what fifty hours of hand-sewing costs.

narration.script: This is the whole subject: two hundred and eighty metres, and you can walk it in three minutes. One block behind Regent Street. Built in the seventeen-thirties as ordinary houses. Nobody planned a tailoring street. Nothing about the street is special. The customers were. Tailors were one street west, dressing the gentry, and they followed them in — a trade cluster, the way Silicon Valley is a cluster. The root here is uniform, not fashion: an army cap-maker of 1771, a navy outfitter of 1785. That shoulder was cut for men who had to ride, march, and be recognised at a distance. Every suit starts as chalk on cloth, cut from a paper pattern made for one person. From seven and a half thousand pounds. An apprentice spends two to six years learning one part of the job. Six years before anyone trusts you with trousers.
